densnv

English | Español

The main goal of densnv is the exploratory analysis of the Vector-Borne Diseases (VBD) and Arthropod Venom Poisoning datasets of the National Epidemiological Surveillance System (SINAVE) of the Ministry of Health of Mexico, through graphs, tables and maps, to support rational and timely decisions in the VBD prevention and control programs.

densnv is part of the dengueverse, a set of R packages for the analysis of dengue transmission in Mexico.

Installation

The development version of densnv is hosted on GitHub and R-universe. It can be installed with pak, remotes or devtools:

# from R-universe (binaries, faster)
install.packages("densnv",
                 repos = c("https://fdzul.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("fdzul/densnv")

Functions

The functions are grouped by prefix:

  • read: load the SINAVE datasets into R (read(), read_dengue_dataset()).

  • cases: aggregate the cases by municipality, locality or epidemiological week (cases_by_agem(), cases_by_loc(), cases_week()).

  • plt: graphs (plt_heatmap(), plt_pyramid(), plt_serotype(), plt_treemap()).

  • mp: static, animated and interactive maps (mp_active_foci(), mp_animated_loc(), mp_animated_mpo(), mp_bumpmap(), mp_cases_loc(), mp_heatmap(), mp_heatmap_edo(), mp_serotype()).

  • tb: tables (tb_conf()).

  • rt: effective reproductive number (rt_dengue()).

  • geocoding: prepare, geocode and save the addresses of the cases (data_geocode(), geocode(), save_geocode()).

Active transmission foci and epidemiological scenarios

mp_active_foci() identifies the active transmission foci with space-time DBSCAN (by default, 3 or more cases within 400 m, the flight range of Aedes aegypti, and within the temporal window), delimits the transmission and control zones and selects the blocks to treat. It also:

  1. Tests the space-time interaction with the Knox test (global and by focus), with Monte Carlo permutations.

  2. Estimates the effective reproductive number (Rt) of the locality with rt_dengue().

  3. Diagnoses the epidemiological scenario (generalised transmission, focalised transmission, focalised transmission with dispersed cases or no active foci) with the criteria of sustained and significant increase, operational capacity and dispersion of the cases, and proposes the operational strategy (focalised strategy, barrido or operativo integral, and early warning).

library(densnv)

res <- mp_active_foci(geocoded_dataset = z,      # geocoded cases (long, lat)
                      cve_edo = "31",
                      locality = "Merida",
                      status_caso = c(1, 2),
                      spatial_scale = 400,
                      temporal_scale = 28,
                      min_cases = 3,
                      buffer_m = 0,
                      ref_date = NULL,
                      method = "st-dbscan",
                      n_sim = 999,
                      perm_days = 365,
                      alpha = 0.05,
                      seed = 123,
                      place = "REP",
                      mean_si = 21,
                      std_si = 6.1,
                      capacity_cases = NULL,
                      coverage_min = NULL,
                      foci_min = 0.9,
                      save = FALSE,
                      dir = "./")

res$foci                   # summary of the active foci
res$blocks                 # blocks to treat
res$knox                   # global Knox test
res$diagnostico$tabla      # scenario, criteria and action
res$diagnostico$rt_plot    # Rt curve

rt_dengue() can also be used on its own, for the country, a state, a municipality or a locality:

rt <- rt_dengue(dataset = dataset,
                level = "state",
                place = "REP",
                cve_edo = "12",
                status_caso = c(1, 2),
                ref_date = NULL,
                period_days = 365,
                window_days = 28,
                mean_si = 21,
                std_si = 6.1,
                plot = TRUE)
rt$rt_ventana

The outputs (scenarios, actions and maps) are in Spanish, the language of the users of the Mexican VBD program.

Credits

The Vector-Borne Diseases (VBD) and Arthropod Venom Poisoning datasets of the National Epidemiological Surveillance System (SINAVE) of the Ministry of Health of Mexico are for the exclusive use of the staff of the State Ministries of Health and of the federal level.

Original shapefiles are created by official government institutions (INEGI & INE).

Methods and packages the functions are based on:

  • DBSCAN: Hahsler M, Piekenbrock M, Doran D (2019). dbscan: Fast Density-Based Clustering with R. Journal of Statistical Software, 91(1), 1-30. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v091.i01

  • Knox test: Knox EG (1964). The detection of space-time interactions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C, 13(1), 25-30.

  • Rt: Cori A, Ferguson NM, Fraser C, Cauchemez S (2013). A new framework and software to estimate time-varying reproduction numbers during epidemics. American Journal of Epidemiology, 178(9), 1505-1512 (EpiEstim).

Inspiration

The package was inspired by the need to support decision making in the dengue prevention and control program, specifically through the identification of the operational scenarios of active transmission.

Help

If you find a bug, please file a minimal reproducible example on GitHub. For questions and other discussions, feel free to contact me (felipe.dzul.m@gmail.com).
